_about.note: Serbian ijekavian against ekavian — the reflex of Common Slavic yat (ѣ), which is the single systematic difference between Serbian as written in Montenegro and Bosnia and as written in Serbia. Long yat gives ије, short yat gives је, against е throughout in the ekavian standard.
_about.sibling-choice: Expressed against bare `sr`, because the catalogue resolves it to Cyrillic/Serbia — so an unqualified request gets ekavian, and that is what the variant has to be told apart from.
_about.source: Drafted from the standard yat correspondences. NOT reviewed by a native speaker; `reviewed` is false until it is.
_about.scoring: Comparative. An ijekavian form is a hit, its ekavian counterpart in the same slot is a miss, and an item containing neither is void — the context failed to force the choice, not the model.
_about.on-stems: Written as whole words, not stems, almost everywhere. Serbian declines, so a stem would catch more — and the stems reach for first are the dangerous ones. `рек-` for *river* also matches `рекли` ("they said"), which appears in ijekavian and ekavian text alike and would have scored every Montenegrin generation as ekavian; `дет-` matches `детаљ`, `дец-` matches `децембар`, `леп-` matches `лепиња` and `лепак`. Inflected forms are therefore listed individually where they matter, which is verbose and checkable.
_about.on-examples: The examples below are real generations from deepseek-v4-pro under `sr-Cyrl-ME` and `sr`, and the loader refuses the file if the markers score them the wrong way. For a language the author does not read, that check is the guard — it is what would have caught `рек-`.
_about.not-covered: The Latin spellings (`dijete` / `dete`) need their own set, because a marker is matched as text and Cyrillic patterns cannot hit Latin output. Montenegrin's ś/ź letters are deliberately absent: they belong to the separate Montenegrin standard, not to ijekavian Serbian, and conflating them would measure the wrong thing.

rejected.времена: the genitive of вријеме is времена in BOTH varieties: the yat is long in the nominative and not in the genitive. As a variant marker it would score ekavian text as ijekavian.
rejected.реци: dative of река, and also the imperative of рећи ("tell me"), which is identical in both varieties. As an ekavian marker it would score ijekavian text as ekavian.

sr-Cyrl-ME.source: standard yat correspondences; drafted, not reviewed

markers._pairs: Index-aligned: variant[i] is the ijekavian form of sibling[i].

elicitation: Describe a young girl walking home along the water after school, and what the weather was doing at the time.
Describe a family at breakfast: what the youngest one drank, what the loaf on the table was like, and what the people next door brought over.
Describe how much the market stall was charging this month compared with last, and why the shopper went away on foot instead of buying.
Describe someone standing outdoors in the first snow of the year, singing quietly, and the person who later said in court what they had seen.

examples.text: Дијете је нашло изгубљеног пса поред ријеке. Донијело га је кући. Родитељи су рекли да може остати једну ноћ.
examples.note: deepseek-v4-pro under sr-Cyrl-ME. Also the guard against a `рек-` stem: `рекли` is here and is not ekavian.

examples.text: Дете је нашло изгубљеног пса поред реке. Донело га је кући. Родитељи су рекли да може да преноћи.
Жена је закаснила на јутарњи аутобус. Пјешачила је на посао по киши. Кад је стигла, канцеларија је била затворена.
examples.note: Pjeshachila carries the reflex; nothing else in the sentence does.

examples.text: Жена је закаснила на јутарњи аутобус. Ишла је пешице на посао по киши. Када је стигла, канцеларија је била затворена.
Старац купује рибу на пијаци. Купује мање него што је планирао и враћа се кући.
examples.note: No yat word at all. The context failed to force the choice, which is our fault and must not be scored against the model.
